memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Laban answered Jacob, 'The women are my daughters, the children are my children, and the flocks are my flocks. All you see is mine. Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine, or about the children they have borne? Come now, let's make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between us.' So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar. He said to his relatives, 'Gather some stones.' So they took stones and piled them in a heap, and they ate there by the heap." - Gen 31:43-46 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Laban cannot really answer Jacob's charges, so he changes course. Still claiming everything as his — "all you see is mine" — he nonetheless recognises he cannot undo what has happened. So he proposes a covenant, and together they build a heap of stones as a witness, then share a meal beside it.

It is worth noticing what happens here. Two men who deeply distrust each other, who have real grievances, choose to stop the conflict and make a peaceful agreement rather than come to blows. It is not a warm reconciliation — there is no falling into each other's arms — but it is a genuine step away from hostility and toward peace.

Sometimes this is the most we can achieve with a difficult person: not full-hearted friendship, but an honest boundary and a truce. That is not failure; it can be wisdom. Scripture says, "as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone" (Rom 12:18) — recognising that peace does not always depend on us alone, and does not always look like closeness.

If there is someone you cannot fully reconcile with, you can still choose peace over war. A clear agreement, a respectful boundary, an end to hostilities — these honour God even when a warm relationship is not possible. Seek peace as far as it lies within your power.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a difficult relationship where I can choose peace over conflict?
2. Do I recognise that a boundary and a truce can be a godly outcome?
3. Where can I take a step away from hostility, as far as it depends on me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to pursue peace as far as it depends on me, even with difficult people. Where full reconciliation is not possible, give me wisdom to set honest boundaries and end hostility. Amen.
